description: One section from one brief. This is the pipeline we ship today, so it is also the baseline every later stage is measured against. Scored with the corrective retry OFF: the retry is what we are trying to stop needing.

cases.prompt: A hero section for a coffee roaster: a headline, one line of copy, and two buttons.
cases.why: The simplest thing anyone will ask for. If this is not perfect, nothing else matters.

cases.prompt: A features section with 3 columns: fast, secure, affordable — each with a heading and a sentence.
cases.why: The most common multi-column shape. Catches column-count and layout-mismatch errors together.

cases.prompt: A three-column features row where each column is a card with an icon above a heading and a short description.
cases.why: info-box IS this card. If the model builds it out of loose columns instead, block choice is the problem, not layout.

cases.prompt: A pricing section with three plans — Starter $9, Team $29, Business $79 — each listing four features and a sign-up button, with Team highlighted as recommended.
cases.why: The brief the whole thing started from. Long, structured, and the one most likely to blow the column caps.

cases.prompt: A call-to-action band: a short headline and a single button, centred, full width.
cases.why: Single column. Checks the model does not invent columns it was not asked for, and that it uses the centre alignment attribute rather than describing centring in the copy.

cases.prompt: A testimonial section with a customer quote and the customer's name and job title underneath.
cases.why: No dedicated quote block exists in the allowlist. Tests whether the model composes one sensibly instead of inventing a block.

cases.prompt: A section with text on the left and an image on the right, roughly 60/40.
cases.why: The one case where setting `layout` explicitly is correct. Checks the unequal-split instruction actually lands.

cases.prompt: A section with an image on the left at 40% and the text on the right at 60%.
cases.why: The mirror of the previous case. A model that has memorised one layout id rather than reading the table will get this wrong.

cases.prompt: A section headed "Everything included" with a tick-list of six benefits underneath.
cases.why: icon-list is exactly this. Another block-choice probe, and it needs icon-list-item children to be legal.

cases.prompt: An FAQ section with four questions and answers.
cases.why: FAQs are the section the v1 allowlist could not build. The accordion is allowlisted now, so flattening Q&A into loose advanced-text blocks is the failure — and the answer must be a child of the item, not the title.

cases.prompt: A row of four statistics: 10,000 customers, 99.9% uptime, 24/7 support, 15 countries.
cases.why: Four columns, very short copy. Checks the four-column layout and that numbers survive into the copy.

cases.prompt: A meet-the-team section with two people, each with a photo, a name, and a one-line bio.
cases.why: Images must be placeholders. Catches invented URLs and attachment ids, which the validator rejects outright.

cases.prompt: A trusted-by strip: a small line of text and five client logos in a row.
cases.why: Five columns is near the cap of six. Checks the model does not exceed it and does not silently drop logos.

cases.prompt: A newsletter sign-up band with a heading, one line of reassurance about spam, and a subscribe button.
cases.why: No form block exists. Correct behaviour is a button; failure is inventing an input block.

cases.prompt: A "how it works" section with three numbered steps, each with a title and a sentence.
cases.why: Numbered ordering. icon-list with iconType=ordered is the designed answer; three columns is acceptable.

cases.prompt: A dark call-to-action section with a bold headline and one button.
cases.why: "Dark" needs a background attribute that is NOT in the allowlist. Tests whether the model degrades gracefully or invents an attribute key.

cases.prompt: An about section: a heading, three paragraphs of real copy about a family-run bakery founded in 1974, and a link to the story.
cases.why: Long-form copy. Checks paragraphs use textHTMLTag p rather than heading tags, and that copy is specific rather than generic.

cases.prompt: Two short paragraphs of terms-and-conditions text with a plain horizontal rule between them and no caption on the rule.
cases.why: separatorLabelEnable must be false or the rule renders the literal word "Separator". A known trap the prompt calls out.

cases.prompt: A row of six small feature tiles, each with just an icon and a word.
cases.why: Exactly at the six-column cap. Checks the boundary is reachable rather than rejected.

cases.prompt: A section with twelve columns, each containing a heading, a paragraph, an image, a list of ten items and three buttons.
cases.why: Deliberately impossible — twelve columns exceeds the cap of six. The right outcome is a sane reduced section, not a validator rejection. This case measures graceful degradation.
